description.text: Established in 1972, Houlihan Lokey, Inc. is a leading global independent investment bank with expertise in mergers and acquisitions (“M&A”), capital markets, financial restructurings, liability management, and financial and valuation advisory services. We serve a diverse set of clients worldwide, including corporations, financial sponsors and government agencies. We provide our financial professionals with an integrated platform that enables them to deliver meaningful and differentiated advice to our clients. We advise our clients on critical strategic and financial decisions, employing a rigorous analytical approach coupled with deep product and industry expertise. We market our services through our product areas, our industry groups and our Financial Sponsors group, serving our clients in three business segments: Corporate Finance (“CF”), encompassing M&A and capital solutions; Financial Restructuring (“FR”), including restructurings both out-of-court and in formal bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings; and Financial and Valuation Advisory (“FVA”), including financial opinions and a variety of valuation and financial consulting services. We are committed to a set of principles that serve as the backbone of our success. Independent advice and intellectual rigor, combined with consistent senior-level involvement, are hallmarks of our commitment to client service.

about.description_short: Houlihan Lokey, Inc. (NYSE:HLI) is a leading global investment bank recognized for delivering independent strategic and financial advice to corporations, financial sponsors, and governments. With uniquely deep industry expertise, broad international reach, and a partnership approach rooted in trust, the firm provides innovative, integrated solutions across mergers and acquisitions, capital solutions, financial restructuring, and financial and valuation advisory. Our unmatched transaction volumes provide differentiated, data-driven perspectives that help our clients achieve their most critical goals.

analysis_md:
# HLI — Houlihan Lokey, Inc.
v5 run (engine release 5.5.0), 2026-10-20. Price $130.33 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $8.919B — in scope (under $40B).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json or statements.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Global independent investment bank built on the mid-market: Corporate Finance (M&A and capital solutions — the majority of engagements are mid-cap transactions the bulge brackets underserve), Financial Restructuring (the No. 1 global restructuring franchise by deal count, eleven years running), and Financial & Valuation Advisory. No. 1 global M&A advisor by transaction count. The three-segment mix is the story: restructuring and valuation work is countercyclical ballast when M&A fees fall. Pure people business — no lending book, no balance-sheet risk, essentially no funded debt.

Revenue by fiscal year (financials_history.csv): FY2022 $2,269,958,000 → FY2023 $1,809,447,000 (deal freeze) → FY2024 $1,914,404,000 → FY2025 $2,389,416,000 → FY2026 $2,617,516,000 (record). Latest quarter, Q1 FY2027 (ended 2026-06-30, per the company's Q1 release): revenue $511 million vs $605 million a year earlier, diluted EPS $1.15 vs $1.42 — Corporate Finance fell to $303 million from $398 million on delayed larger-fee closings (Middle East instability, software-sector disruption as AI repriced tech deals); management calls the headwind temporary, says delayed deals remain in the pipeline, and guides the FY2027 adjusted compensation ratio to the 61.5% long-term target.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2026 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $704,131,000; capex $22,312,000 (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, rollup); SBC $201,304,000 (AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense — always a real cost here; it is how the bankers are paid).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2026: $480,515,000 = $7.02/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $7.02; latest FY OE total $480.5M; shares diluted 68,434,896).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC, financials_history.csv): $446,019,000 — same ballpark as the conservative figure, which raises confidence.
- The three base-window years show the cycle in full: FY2024 OE/share $1.40 (OE total $95,133,000), FY2025 $9.33 ($640,467,000), FY2026 $7.02 ($480,515,000). OE positive 4 of the last 5 fiscal years (key_numbers.md) — the exception is FY2023 (OE total −$71,394,000), when OCF collapsed to $136,273,000 on the deal freeze while SBC ran $156,936,000.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base, $7.02/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; the median of $1.40 / $9.33 / $7.02 is the FY2026 figure itself). No STALE_FY flag fired (6.7 months since FY end), so the median base stands by design — it is the through-cycle normalizer for exactly this kind of filer.
- **TTM check (ttm.py, filing-direct):** OCF: FY $704,131,000 − prior YTD −$132,000,000 + current YTD −$336,000,000 = **TTM $500,131,000**; capex: FY $22,312,000 − prior YTD $13,000,000 + current YTD $6,000,000 = **TTM $15,312,000**; SBC: FY $201,304,000 − prior YTD $42,000,000 + current YTD $45,000,000 = **TTM $204,304,000**; shares (current-YTD weighted diluted) **67,600,000**; **TTM OE total $280,515,000 → $4.15/share**. The TTM is NOT used as the base: Q1 is the annual bonus-payment quarter (OCF is negative in Q1 every year — −$132,000,000 in Q1 FY2026, −$336,000,000 in Q1 FY2027 on the larger FY2026 bonus pool), so the TTM swap replaces one bonus quarter with a much larger one at the same moment Q1 revenue fell 15.6%. It is quoted here as the current run-rate warning the bear cases are built on, not as normalized earnings power — the platform that produced record FY2025–26 revenue (record managing-director count, two acquisitions closed in Q4 FY2026) is larger than the one the FY2024 trough year in the median window reflects.
- No overrides of any kind. No tier_override — see SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH below for why the insurer/bank notch does not apply to a fee-only advisor.

## Moat: 6/10 — moderate, the top of the band
Justification: No. 1 global M&A advisor by deal count and No. 1 global restructuring franchise, with a three-segment mix (Corporate Finance, countercyclical Financial Restructuring, Financial & Valuation Advisory) that kept ROIC at 24–35% in every one of the last five fiscal years including the FY2023–24 deal trough — but it is a people business: no contracts or switching costs per mandate, managing directors can walk, and a ~61.5% compensation ratio means the bankers capture most of the economics.
- FOR: No. 1 global M&A advisor by transaction count and No. 1 global restructuring franchise (11 years) — scale and reputation in the mid-market segment bulge brackets underserve; countercyclical mix: restructuring and valuation work offsets M&A downturns (FY2023 revenue fell 20% while M&A froze, and the firm stayed solidly profitable); ROIC proxy 24.0–34.5% across FY2024–26 and 29.8% even in trough FY2023 — returns stayed well above cost of capital through the cycle; asset-light, debt-free balance sheet: $1,189,454,000 cash at FY2026 against no filed funded debt — no balance-sheet risk to the franchise; gross margin held in a 29.8–35.0% band over FY2022–25 despite the cycle — fee pricing power in its niches.
- AGAINST: People business: clients hire individuals, not the platform — managing-director departures take revenue with them and there are no contracts or switching costs per mandate; bankers capture the economics: adjusted compensation ratio guided to the 61.5% long-term target for FY2027, capping shareholder margin leverage; deal fees are cyclical and closing-dependent: Q1 FY2027 Corporate Finance revenue fell to $303M from $398M on delayed larger-fee closings (Middle East instability, software-sector disruption); intense competition from bulge brackets moving downmarket and boutiques (Evercore, Moelis, Lazard) moving into the mid-market; stock compensation is large and rising ($201,304,000 in FY2026) — a real, recurring cost of retaining the talent that is the moat.
- Evidence (fundamentals.json `roic_proxy`, after-tax operating income over equity + debt − cash): FY2022 72.9% (peak operating income on a small net invested-capital base), FY2023 29.8%, FY2024 24.0%, FY2025 31.4%, FY2026 34.5% — never below 24% in any year, trough included; that through-cycle return record is what carries the score to 6 rather than the 5 the closest scored peer (Evercore) carries. Gross margin (fundamentals.json): FY2022 35.04%, FY2023 30.79%, FY2024 29.83%, FY2025 32.32%; FY2026 gross profit is not tagged in the filing feed (fundamentals.json carries no FY2026 gross margin), so the margin evidence stops at FY2025 — operating margin FY2026 was 20.13% vs 21.03% in FY2025.
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 9.8 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-20)
**Growth sanity check (mandatory):** the engine's blended start is 11.83% (components: rev CAGR 5y 11.40%, rev CAGR 3y 13.09%, latest rev YoY 9.55%, OE/share CAGR 2y 124.42% — the last is a trough artifact off FY2024's $1.40/share and is not a growth rate any scenario uses). Against the actual prints — FY2026 revenue +9.55%, FY2025 revenue +24.81%, Q1 FY2027 revenue $511 million vs $605 million (−15.6%), TTM OE $4.15/share vs the $7.02 base — an 11.83% base start would assume the Q1 FY2027 Corporate Finance delay headwind is already over. It is not, per management's own Q1 call. Scenario starts were therefore recalibrated down via offsets (−13.83 / −8.83 / −4.83 / +0.17 / +5.17pp vs the blend) to −2 / +3 / **+7** / +12 / +17%. The base start (7%) sits below the FY2026 print for the written reason above and above the TTM revenue trend because delayed deals are described as delayed, not lost, with restructuring expectations for FY2027 improved. The bull (12%) and super-bull (17%) starts sit below what the company actually printed in FY2025 (+24.81%) — deliberate: those were catch-up years off the FY2023–24 trough on a smaller platform. Probabilities were shifted to the bear end per OE_VOLATILE (15/30/30/17/8 vs the 10/25/30/25/10 default), and the super-bear/bear OE multipliers cut to 0.65/0.85 (FY2023 printed negative OE; a repeat deal freeze on today's larger, record-headcount cost base lands in that zone).

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | -2.0% | 0.65 | FY2023-style deal freeze repeats; record MD cost base meets falling fees | $30.64 | 5.27% |
| Bear | 30% | 3.0% | 0.85 | Delays persist through FY2027; restructuring offsets only part of the Corporate Finance hole | $50.05 | 7.32% |
| Base | 30% | 7.0% | 1.00 | Delayed deals close over FY2027–28; mid-single-digit platform growth resumes | $70.35 | 9.44% |
| Bull | 17% | 12.0% | 1.10 | Backlog converts fast; restructuring runs elevated at the same time | $96.63 | 12.04% |
| Super bull | 8% | 17.0% | 1.20 | Full M&A cycle upswing on the enlarged platform | $131.50 | 15.10% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $67.66 (−48.1% vs price), IV@12% $90.60, weighted IRR 9.23%, base-case IRR 9.44%** (key_numbers.md).
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 5.39%, terminal value 19.6% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.29x, 6.7 months since FY end. Even the super-bull case (8%) only just reaches the $130.33 price ($131.50 IV@15%, 15.10% IRR).

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years — in fact $−1.06 to $9.33 across FY2022–26): real and structural — this is a deal-cycle business with a fixed people cost base. Handled as the flag directs: the normalized median base (not the FY2025 peak, not a single year) plus bear-end weighting — 45% of probability sits on bear-or-worse, super-bear/bear multipliers cut to 0.65/0.85.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (FY2025: net income $399,711,000 vs OCF $848,609,000): the one-off is compensation timing on a fee surge, not earnings quality. statements.json's FY2025 cash-flow lines identify non-cash stock compensation of $168,443,000 and depreciation & amortization of $41,270,000 added back to net income, plus a $55,698,000 inflow from receivables collection; the balance of the gap is the accrued-compensation build on FY2025's +24.81% revenue year — bonuses accrued at March 31, 2025 and cash-paid in Q1 FY2026, a build the standardized statements do not break out as a separate line. Consequence: FY2025's $9.33 OE/share is flattered by timing, FY2026 partly reverses it (OCF $704,131,000 on net income $425,697,000), and the 3-year median base is the right antidote — one more reason the base is the median, not FY2025.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK** (no debt tag for the latest fiscal year — net debt unknown to the engine): resolved from the filing (statements.json / fundamentals.json).
